E1.evidence: Issue gives configuration, a video, and a code-level diagnosis; maintainer SteveMacenski engaged and proposed the fix direction: "Maybe we should check the `obstacle_max_range` in grid cell space then, no? I think that would resolve the issue so that they're all working on the same discretized space." (https://github.com/ros-navigation/navigation2/issues/5476#issuecomment-3250374983). Fixed by merged PR #5697 (main) and backport #5775 (jazzy).

E2.evidence: The defect is an inconsistency between two computations inside the ObstacleLayer: marking compares the metric point distance with obstacle_max_range while clearing raytraces in discretized cells up to raytrace_max_range. Reporter: "When evaluating whether a cell should be marked, it uses the actual point distance compared to the `obstacle_max_range`" / "When evaluating the grid cell to clear up to, it takes the last _cell_ which `min(raytrace_max_range, point_distance)`  lies within" (https://github.com/ros-navigation/navigation2/issues/5476#issuecomment-3248253572). PR #5697: "When marking obstacles from new observations, the check against `obstacle_max_range` is done in grid cell space for consistency with the ray tracing free space check  against `raytrace_max_range`". Only nav2_costmap_2d/plugins/obstacle_layer.cpp (and tests) change. The scan data crossing the boundary is correct; any correct scan source produces the same clearing.

E3.evidence: Would be PAIR (scan source feeds the obstacle layer). Not decisive because the case stops at E2.

E4.evidence: Observed wrong costmap content: "when reversing away from an obstacle, as it moves outside the `obstacle_max_range`, the obstacle is cleared away instead of persisting."

notes: Reported on Jazzy binaries (ros-jazzy-navigation2 1.3.7). PR #5697 also excludes the observation cell from raytracing; the jazzy backport #5775 carries only the grid-space obstacle_max_range check. The obstacle_max_range/raytrace_max_range parameters are the layer's own configuration, not an interface to another unit.
